items.stem:
Mishra Retail Ltd has a current ratio of 4:1 while the industry average is 2:1. Its managers believe this shows excellent performance. Its inventory turnover is much lower than its rivals'.
(i) Is the high current ratio necessarily good? Explain. (ii) Which limitation of ratio analysis should the managers remember?
items.answer: (i) No: it may indicate idle funds, excess inventory or slow collection. (ii) Ratios are only indicators; there is no universal ideal ratio and they ignore qualitative factors (any one with explanation).

items.stem: Find the quick ratio from: inventories ₹3,60,000, trade receivables ₹2,70,000, cash and cash equivalents ₹1,10,000, current liabilities ₹7,00,000.
items.markingKey: (b) Current assets ₹7,40,000; current ratio = ₹7,40,000/₹7,00,000 = 1.06:1. Quick assets = ₹7,40,000 − inventories ₹3,60,000 = ₹3,80,000; quick ratio = 0.54:1.
options: Quick ratio 1.84:1

items.stem: The quick ratio of a company is 0.72:1 (current assets ₹5,80,000, quick assets ₹2,80,000, current liabilities ₹3,90,000). Transaction: Collected ₹1,45,000 from trade receivables. The quick ratio will increase, decrease or not change? Give reasons with calculation.
items.markingKey: Identification 1 mark; calculation and reason 2 marks: quick ratio = 0.72:1 (was 0.72:1): no change.
